title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated video was used to clone the identity of a real, named immigration attorney and deploy that likeness in fake social media advertisements. The failure did not occur inside a legitimate AI product but in the use of AI as a tool by external actors to manufacture a convincing false persona at scale. The volume reported, more than 8,000 fake profile videos, indicates the cloning was systematic rather than opportunistic, and the fraud exploited a population with a specific legal vulnerability and limited institutional support.

The scam succeeded at several points where a check could have interrupted it: the social media platform did not prevent the fake ads from running, the payment app processed multiple transfers without triggering a fraud alert, and the victim had no accessible way to verify the attorney's identity before sending documents and money. The collection of government identity documents alongside the financial loss created a second harm, ongoing identity-theft risk, that persists after the fraud itself was discovered.

What is not established is who is responsible for creating or distributing the fake videos, whether law enforcement has identified any suspect, or whether any platform has been found liable for hosting the content.

reports.title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A legal resident from the Bronx lost $4,820 to scammers using artificial intelligence after responding to a fake social media ad promising citizenship help without an exam. Victor Hernandez, who has lived in the United States for over a decade, was tricked into sending personal documents including his Social Security card and residency card through multiple payment requests via the money transfer app Zelle. The scam only became apparent when his wife suggested something seemed wrong and they consulted a friend.

The fake advertisement used AI technology to impersonate real immigration attorney Angel Leal from Miami, whose identity was cloned without his knowledge. Leal discovered his image had been used to create over 8,000 fake profile videos targeting immigrants nationwide. After the scam was discovered, the perpetrators attempted to extort additional money from Hernandez. He has filed reports with police and federal law enforcement but remains worried about identity theft, as he provided all his personal information to the criminals. Leal warns people to avoid hiring attorneys based on social media ads and to be suspicious of anyone requesting payment through cash-sending apps.
